tier_reason: First-party author blog post (Rusty Russell, November 2010) comparing JudyL against htable at three densities; the post is EGRESS_BLOCKED here and search snippets confirm only the setup (50,000,000 objects, ns per operation, 75 percent dense, 37 percent sparse, 37 percent with bit-stealing disabled), not the numbers. No CPU, compiler or flags are known for the post and the repo carries no Judy harness, so it cannot reach A or B.

corrections.caveats: Snippet only: rusty.ozlabs.org was EGRESS_BLOCKED for both the search agent and the verifier, so the post was never opened; web-search snippets confirm the post exists and its setup (JudyL vs htable at 75 percent full, 37 percent full and 37 percent full with bit-stealing disabled, 50,000,000 objects, total time divided by object count), but the specific ns figures in claimed_speedup come from an earlier search summary and were not seen by the verifier. Machine, CPU, compiler and flags of the post are unknown. First-party author blog post from November 2010, on code changed many times since (htable commits through 2026). The repo's ccan/htable/tools/speed.c times htable alone (its only Judy reference is a comment that in-order lookups are cache-friendly for Judy), so the Judy comparison is not reproducible from the repo. ccan/htable/tools/hsearchspeed.c does time glibc hsearch(3) on the same /usr/share/dict/words string workload as stringspeed.c (Makefile: -Wall -Werror -O3), so an htable vs libc hsearch comparison can be run from the repo, but no result numbers are published anywhere in the repo. Judy is a strong incumbent but not a standard-library facility, and the win is only on random-access lookups, not on inserts or sequential (in-order) access. No other numeric comparison found for any CCAN module.

notes: Real, notable module (CCAN 1.2k stars, htable vendored in Samba); tier C stands, but the quoted ns numbers are unverified (benchmark post blocked, snippets confirm setup only). Shortcomings: first-party 2010 blog numbers with no hardware/compiler/flags, Judy comparison not reproducible from the repo, htable wins only random lookups and loses inserts and in-order lookups to Judy; repo ships an hsearch(3) harness (hsearchspeed.c vs stringspeed.c) but no published results. License LGPL-2.1-or-later confirmed from ccan/htable/_info; last commit 2026-09-14 confirmed.
